title: Change One Number, Sum a Range

concept.title: A Fenwick tree stores partial sums so that both an update and a prefix sum take about log n steps
body: A row of `n` numbers is given, and then `q` operations come in turn. Some operations **change one number**, others ask for the **sum of a range**. For the row `5 1 4 2` the sum of the cells 2 to 4 is 7; after adding 10 to the cell 3 it is 17. If each sum is computed with a loop, the work is O(n) per question, up to 9 * 10^8 steps in total. If every sum is read from a table of prefix sums, an update would have to rebuild the table, which is O(n) again.

A **Fenwick tree** (also called a *binary indexed tree*) keeps a clever array `t` in which the cell `t[i]` holds the sum of the **last `i & -i` numbers** ending at the position `i` (the expression `i & -i` is the lowest set bit of `i`: for `i = 12 = 1100` it is `4`, so `t[12]` covers the cells 9 to 12). To get the sum of the first `i` numbers, add `t[i]`, then jump to `i - (i & -i)` and add again, until `i` is 0: each jump clears the lowest set bit, so there are at most log n jumps. To add `x` to the cell `i`, update every `t[j]` that covers `i`: start at `i` and jump to `j + (j & -j)` until `j` passes `n`.

body.code:
def add(t, i, x):                 # the number at the position i grows by x
    while i <= n:
        t[i] += x
        i += i & -i               # the next cell that covers the position i

def prefix(t, i):                 # the sum of the first i numbers
    s = 0
    while i > 0:
        s += t[i]
        i -= i & -i               # remove the lowest set bit
    return s

# a range sum is the difference of two prefix sums
answer = prefix(t, y) - prefix(t, x - 1)

body: A range sum is `prefix(y) - prefix(x - 1)`, the same difference trick as for prefix sums. To build the tree start from zeros and add every number with `add` (O(n log n)). Every operation takes O(log n) time, so the whole input is processed in O((n + q) log n). The sums here reach about 10^15, so use 64-bit numbers.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` adds `y` to the number at the position `x`; type 2 `x y` asks for the sum of the numbers at the positions `x` to `y`. Print the answers to all the questions of type 2 on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, add `y` to the cell number `x`. If `t = 2`, print the sum of the cells from `x` to `y`.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: |each cell| <= 10^6 at the start, |y| <= 10^6 in the additions
Cells are numbered from 1; for a sum 1 <= x <= y <= n.

examples.note: 1 + 4 + 2 = 7; after adding 10 to the third number: 1 + 14 + 2 = 17; the whole row: 5 + 1 + 14 + 2 = 22.

hints: Keep a Fenwick tree; t[i] covers the last i & -i positions ending at i.
To add, move up with i += i & -i; to sum a prefix, move down with i -= i & -i.
A range sum is the difference of two prefix sums.
